title: Diagonal projective embedding of a normal quasi-projective split-torus scheme over a ring
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $r\geq0$, and $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r=\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, the base change to $S$ of the split torus of [def-sc-gm-ga]: its coordinate ring has $A$-basis the Laurent monomials $t^w=\prod_{
u=1}^rt_
u^{w_
u}$ ($w\in\mathbf Z^r$) with $t^wt^{w'}=t^{w+w'}$, and its group law is given by $t_
u\mapsto t_
u\otimes t_
u$, counit $t_
u\mapsto1$ and antipode $t_
u\mapsto t_
u^{-1}$ (for $r=0$, $T=S$). Let $X	o S$ be a separated finite-type scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with every local ring an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose $X$ is quasi-projective over $S$, meaning it admits an $S$-immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[z_0,\ldots,z_N]$ with the total-degree grading [def-pc-proj, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $a:T	imes_SX	o X$ be an action [def-pc-fibre-product], satisfying the unit and associativity identities as scheme-morphism equalities. Then there are $n\geq0$, weights $w_0,\ldots,w_n\in\mathbf Z^r$, and a $T$-equivariant $S$-immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_A$. The action on this projective space is specified by the graded algebra coaction
$$A[z_0,\ldots,z_n]\longrightarrow A[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}][z_0,\ldots,z_n],\qquad z_i\longmapsto t^{w_i}z_i,\quad a\longmapsto a\ (a\in A),$$
where $t^w=\prod_{
u=1}^rt_
u^{w_
u}$ and the displayed map determines the projective action by pullback of homogeneous coordinates. Equivariance is equality of scheme morphisms, including after every base change. Empty $X$, $r=0$, nonreduced $A$, and disconnected $X$ are allowed.

source.place: WANTED local copy. R. W. Thomason, Equivariant resolution, linearization, and Hilbert's fourteenth problem over arbitrary base schemes, Adv. Math. 65 (1987), Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4(3), printed p.32; read primary article full text online at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/243015730_Equivariant_resolution_linearization_and_Hilbert%27s_fourteenth_problem_over_arbitrary_base_schemes . Split-torus diagonal free enlargement of its equivariant vector bundle is the agent's ring-coefficient consequence; no Stacks tag is claimed for the linearization theorem.

proof.text: Let $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_A$ be the immersion in the hypotheses and put $L_0=i^*\mathcal O(1)$. The canonical twist and quotient on projective space of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] make $L_0$ relatively very ample by [def-trf-relatively-very-ample]. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-normal-line-power-linearization] to obtain $m\geq1$ and a linearization of $L_0^{\otimes m}$. Its assumptions are exactly the given normality of $X$, separated finite type over the Noetherian affine base, and the split-torus action; no normality of the base is needed.

source.place: WANTED local copy. R. W. Thomason, Equivariant resolution, linearization, and Hilbert's fourteenth problem over arbitrary base schemes, Adv. Math. 65 (1987), proof of Theorem 3.3, printed p.32, first paragraph: the positive-power linearization input before choosing a coherent submodule of sections. Read primary article online at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/243015730_Equivariant_resolution_linearization_and_Hilbert%27s_fourteenth_problem_over_arbitrary_base_schemes . This is the split-torus case of that input; no Stacks tag is asserted for this theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-relative-ample-very-ample], relative very ampleness of $L_0$ implies that $L_0^{\otimes d}$ is relatively very ample for every sufficiently large $d$. Choose $d=mk$ in that range with $k\geq1$ and set $L=L_0^{\otimes mk}$. Tensoring the preceding linearization $k$ times gives a linearization $\theta$ of $L$: identity and cocycle follow by tensoring those same equalities. Apply [lem-sfb-very-ample-affine-finite-sections] to obtain sections $s_0,\ldots,s_N$ generating $L$ whose quotient defines an immersion $i_s:X\to\mathbf P^N_A$. Finite type and affine base are precisely the hypotheses for this finite section system.

Use [lem-sfb-relative-linearized-line-sections-coaction] for $(X,L,\theta)$ and write $c(s_i)=\sum_u s_{i,u}\otimes t^u$, with finite support. Comparing the $t^u$ coefficients in $(c\otimes1)c(s_i)=(1\otimes\Delta)c(s_i)$ gives $c(s_{i,u})=s_{i,u}\otimes t^u$; the counit gives $s_i=\sum_u s_{i,u}$. Thus the finitely many coefficients $v_0,\ldots,v_n$ of these finitely many sums still generate $L$. Assign to each $v_j$ its exponent $u_j$. Append a zero section with exponent zero if necessary so the list is nonempty. This comparison uses the stated Laurent monomial basis over $A$, so works with torsion and nilpotents and uses no eigenbasis over a field.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero for the flat Laurent algebra C and its tensor square. The normalized section coaction is an agent-formulated consequence of that base-change map and the explicit linearization identity and cocycle, not a verbatim assertion of 02KH.

proof.text: The quotient $q:f^*\mathcal O_S^{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow L$, $e_j\mapsto v_j$, classifies an $S$-morphism $j:X\to\mathbf P^n_A$ by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. To verify that $j$ is an immersion, define $\alpha:\mathcal O_S^{N+1}\to\mathcal O_S^{n+1}$ by sending $e_i$ to the sum of the basis vectors for the coefficients of $s_i$. Then $q\circ f^*\alpha$ is the old quotient defining $i_s$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-quotient-comparison] with its single base open $S$, $E=\mathcal O_S^{N+1}$ and $F=\mathcal O_S^{n+1}$. Its old quotient is surjective and its old classifying map is the immersion $i_s$, so its conclusion is that $j$ is an immersion. This does not assert that adding sections gives a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 01VR, lemma-relatively-very-ample, proof (2) implies (4), comparison of the quotient with a finite immersion system; Constructions Tags 01OA and 01OE for quotient classification and free projective space.

proof.text: Set $w_j=-u_j$. For every $A$-algebra $B$ and $g\in T(B)$, the normalization in [lem-sfb-relative-linearized-line-sections-coaction] gives $\theta_{g,x}(v_j(x))=g^{u_j}v_j(gx)$, hence $v_j(gx)=g^{w_j}\theta_{g,x}(v_j(x))$. This is an equality of pulled-back sections on the test scheme. Under quotient classification [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], the common line isomorphism $\theta_{g,x}$ identifies the coordinates of $j(gx)$ with $(g^{w_j}v_j(x))_j$. The substitution $z_j\mapsto t^{w_j}z_j$, fixing $A$, therefore gives exactly the required projective action and makes $j$ equivariant. On generators its identity and product laws are $1^{w_j}=1$ and $(gh)^{w_j}=g^{w_j}h^{w_j}$. Quotient classification is natural under arbitrary pullback, so the equality holds as scheme morphisms and after any base change, including nonflat or nonreduced tests. For $r=0$ all weights are zero. For empty $X$ the nonempty zero-section list defines its unique immersion, including when $A$ is the zero ring; none of the preceding arguments selects a connected component.

from.place: Relative torus quotient input: invariant affine covering of the normal ample source after finite étale splitting of the torus. This is the relative-base replacement for the field-only Sumihiro lemma. Supporting input: Equivariant projective embedding before selecting boundary-avoiding weight charts.

split_report.summary: Retained the ring-base statement. Split the proof through relative positive-power linearization and the relative section coaction, then constructed finitely many weight sections and used the existing quotient-comparison theorem to preserve immersion. Checked inverse signs on coordinate weights and arbitrary base-change equality; no field-only lemma was applied over A.

tool_uses.why: Canonical invertible-quotient classification and free projective space; needed to define the coordinate morphisms and compare their universal quotients.
Uses the existing relative very-ampleness notion, not the proper-over-field convention.
Choose a sufficiently large multiple of the linearization exponent that is still relatively very ample.
Adding finitely many homogeneous sections preserves the immersion, by comparison with the original quotient.

Item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to clones/live. Live and side-live still show the item unsplit, and there is no repair note. Step 1: L0=i^*O(1) is relatively very ample by def-trf-relatively-very-ample with E=O^{N+1}, using the P(O^{N+1})=P^N_A identification in lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry. The new linearization node's hypotheses (A Noetherian, X normal, separated, finite type) all hold. Step 2: lem-trf-relative-ample-very-ample (01VU) makes every large power very ample, so L=L0^{mk}; the tensor power of the linearization is still one; lem-sfb-very-ample-affine-finite-sections (02NP) applies over the affine base for a finite-type map. Step 3: comparing t^u coefficients over the free Laurent basis gives c(s_u)=s_u⊗t^u, and the counit gives s=Σs_u; elementary and correct, with v_j indexed by the pairs (i,u). Step 4: lem-trf-projective-quotient-comparison with the single open S, E=O^{N+1}, F=O^{n+1} and α(e_i)=sum of the e_j coming from s_i; q∘α is the old immersion quotient, so j is an immersion. Step 5: sign checked, θ(p2^*v_j)=t^{u_j}a^*v_j on T×X, so w_j=-u_j makes the quotients of j∘a and ρ∘(1×j) agree, and classification gives equality of morphisms. New nodes: (1) relative-normal-line-power-linearization is true, even with m=1, because Pic(X×G_m^r)=Pic(X) for normal Noetherian X and units of O(X_i)[s^±,t^±] are u·s^a·t^b, so the cocycle defect is 1. It is not a duplicate: the existing lem-sfb-normal-line-bundle-power-linearization is over an algebraically closed field, and the item has no linearization clause. (2) relative-linearized-line-sections-coaction is true via c=(1⊗S)θ^{-1}(a^*s) in Γ(T×X,p2^*L)=V⊗C (C free, X quasi-compact); g·s is a left action by the cocycle law. It is not a duplicate: the existing coaction nodes are over a field. Both new nodes are statement-only and self-contained, carry 5 recorded Mathlib searches and blueprint fields, and have no cycle.
